chapter: Billie Holiday, Basie leadership and studio work
title: Buddy Collette, Jerry Fielding and breaking studio barriers
summary: Royal was Jerry Fielding's first black studio hire, and Collette got the Groucho Marx show when Royal could not play flute.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: (Inaudible) the first regularly employed black musician in television here was Buddy Collette, wasn't it? On the Groucho Marx Show?
He took the Groucho Marx show because I

couldn't play flute. The fellow that was the leader of that, the music director, had hired me first as sub for Skeets Herford (PHONETIC) on the Hardy Family series, which was radio. At the time of the amalgamation of the locals, that's when pressure started coming in for black guys to get some of the work. The fellow that was the leader of this -- you can think of his name right now. He -- his name actually was Jerry Fielding (PHONETIC). Jerry Fielding was one of the guys that fostered the getting together of black guys in the studios and stuck his neck out. He stuck his neck out for a whole lot of things and he was accused quite wrongly of being a Communist and they tried to do him up in Hollywood and put him on the black list and he was no more Communist than Franklin D. Roosevelt.

He was just a fair man that wanted to do things the way things were supposed to be done and he was -- I was the first guy that he gave a job out there as a black guy, working with the regular studio orchestra. That was for NBC, I believe it was, the Hardy Family, the Mickey Rooney thing.

So, when he went to put his things together, he needed somebody to play on there that also played flute, because there was one place in the title music that played flute and Buddy, though the -- they had several rehearsal bands that were put up at that time, where the white guys were supposed to help the black guys to learn how to do the business and Buddy got inter-

ested in that because he had started learning flute after coming out of the Navy and at that time, he wasn't a hell of a flute player, but he could play enough to make it and Jerry Fielding gave him the job, which I thank him very much for.
